proposed_comments.title: Initialize WinRT before BugReportTool uses it

confidence.rationale: The production entry point reaches WinRT globalization and JSON APIs without apartment initialization; the test fixture initializes it explicitly.

proposed_comments.body:
### Initialize WinRT before BugReportTool uses it

**Severity:** `medium`

**Affected code:** `wmain`, `ReportWindowsSettings`, and the `diagnostic_privacy::sanitize_report` call in `tools/BugReportTool/BugReportTool/Main.cpp`.

**Problem:** `wmain` does not initialize a WinRT apartment, yet `ReportWindowsSettings` calls WinRT globalization APIs and the sanitizer invokes WinRT JSON parsing. The former catches and hides failures; the sanitizer's outer catch deletes the report directory and returns failure.

**Why it matters:** A missing apartment can turn the privacy pass into a hard failure that prevents the bug-report ZIP from being produced.

**Suggested change:** Initialize a WinRT apartment at the beginning of `wmain`, before any WinRT caller, and pair it with scope-bound `winrt::uninit_apartment()`.

**Verification:** At exact head `873e0361b36333bdcae5552933dea675a590db25`, `wmain` still has no apartment initialization: it calls `ReportWindowsSettings` and later `sanitize_report`; `JsonValue::TryParse` is used by the sanitizer. The test fixture initializes WinRT explicitly. No production-entry-point runtime test covers missing initialization.

proposed_comments.title: Terminate and reap the extractor on timeout

confidence.rationale: The current helper launches tar.exe and asserts the 30-second wait result without timeout cleanup; no current test exercises a hung child.

proposed_comments.body:
### Terminate and reap the extractor on timeout

**Severity:** `low`

**Affected code:** `DiagnosticPrivacyTests.cpp`'s `ExtractArchive` helper at the 30-second `WaitForSingleObject` call.

**Problem:** If the wait returns `WAIT_TIMEOUT`, the immediately following assertion fails without terminating or waiting for the launched `tar.exe` process.

**Why it matters:** A timed-out extractor can continue running after its test fails and keep using the temporary archive or directory while later tests proceed.

**Suggested change:** Save the wait result; on `WAIT_TIMEOUT`, terminate the child and wait until it is signaled before asserting. Read its exit code only after `WAIT_OBJECT_0`.

**Verification:** At exact head `873e0361b36333bdcae5552933dea675a590db25`, `ExtractArchive` still asserts `WAIT_OBJECT_0` at line 891 and then reads the exit code; it has no timeout-specific termination or reaping. The added read-only-file tests do not exercise a hung child.

proposed_comments.title: Preserve the cause when report sanitization fails

confidence.rationale: The exact-head sanitizer has throwing I/O, WinRT parsing, and newly added file-attribute checks, while its outer catch discards all exception details.

proposed_comments.body:
### Preserve the cause when report sanitization fails

**Severity:** `low`

**Affected code:** The catch-all around `diagnostic_privacy::sanitize_report` in `tools/BugReportTool/BugReportTool/Main.cpp`.

**Problem:** Exceptions from WinRT parsing, file I/O, or the new staged-file attribute checks are discarded, and the tool prints the same generic message before returning failure. Scope-exit cleanup then attempts to remove the staging directory without exposing the original error.

**Why it matters:** When no ZIP is created, users and maintainers cannot distinguish an access-denied attribute change from a parsing or other file error, making the failure harder to diagnose.

**Suggested change:** Preserve a sanitized error category or HRESULT for expected WinRT/filesystem failures, with a generic fallback for unknown exceptions. Keep the existing fail-closed behavior and cleanup; do not log report contents or sensitive paths.

**Verification:** At exact head `873e0361b36333bdcae5552933dea675a590db25`, `sanitize_report` uses throwing streams and WinRT JSON parsing, and now checks `GetFileAttributesW`/`SetFileAttributesW` through `winrt::check_bool`; `wmain` still catches everything and prints only the generic failure. No runtime failure was triggered to test user-visible diagnostics.
